userStories.title: M1 startup registration — ProvisionBundledAppsCommand (app:provision-bundled) + BUNDLED source type + entrypoint.sh integration

userStories.completionNotes: Done. Commits 5bfe5bef + a437674f. ApplicationRegistrationSourceType.BUNDLED enum value; ApplicationRegistrationEntity.bundledAppSourcePath nullable text column with @WasIntroducedInUpgrade; 2-39 instance command (1789905000000) ADD COLUMN; ApplicationPackageFetcherService BUNDLED case resolves from FS path; ProvisionBundledAppsCommand (app:provision-bundled): reads *.tgz from BUNDLED_APPS_DIR, registers with sourceType=BUNDLED/isPreInstalled=true/ownerWorkspaceId=null, idempotent, --dry-run; DatabaseCommandModule wired; entrypoint.sh calls provision_bundled_apps() after setup_and_migrate_db (provision-bundled then install-pre-installed-apps); PreInstalledAppsService.installOnWorkspace improved (APP_ALREADY_INSTALLED no longer error-logs); 5-case spec file. Tier-2 residual: live Docker boot registering 5 apps + installing on all workspaces.

userStories.title: M1(e) upgrade cursor reachability — resume at an instance command inserted behind an applied workspace segment
userStories.description: As an operator upgrading an instance already at the 2.39.0 workspace segment to an image carrying the new AddBundledAppSourcePath instance command, I want `upgrade` to run that instance command once without re-running the applied workspace segment, so that the bundled-app column exists and boot stays idempotent.
userStories.completionNotes: Executor done (awaiting orchestrator). UpgradeSequenceRunnerService.resolveStartCursor: workspace last-attempted cursor now resumes at the first unattempted instance command of the instance block preceding the workspace segment (getLastAttemptedInstanceCommand index + 1; whole block when the instance cursor is before it) instead of the segment start. Second defect found while fixing: running such a late instance command wrote workspace-scoped rows that became each workspace's newest cursor, re-queuing the entire applied 2.39.0 workspace segment on the next boot — InstanceCommandRunnerService now skips workspace rows for workspaces whose cursor is already past the step (workspaceIdsPastThisStep). Barrier enforcement accepts cursors past the barrier (also fixes retrying a failed instance step that directly follows a workspace segment, which previously threw). Specs: unit upgrade-sequence-runner-inserted-instance-command.spec.ts (6 cases, mocked services), exclude-workspace-ids.util.spec.ts (3), integration inserted-instance-command.integration-spec.ts (4 cases incl. second-boot no-op). No committed 2-39 file touched, no renumbering. Tier-2 residual: on the dev DB with both workspaces at index 328, `upgrade` runs AddBundledAppSourcePath once (instance row only) and a second `upgrade` is a no-op.

userStories.title: Install log hygiene — refuse an already-installed version before any state change (no ERROR on every boot)
userStories.description: As an operator watching boot logs, I want `install-pre-installed-apps` to report already-installed bundled apps at info level only, so that real install failures are not buried under one ERROR per app per workspace per boot.
userStories.completionNotes: Executor done (awaiting orchestrator). ApplicationInstallService.runInstall: for an INSTALLED application the version-progression check now runs before the UPGRADING state flip and outside the rollback try/catch (new private assertInstallVersionProgressionAllowed). SAME_VERSION → APP_ALREADY_INSTALLED thrown with no log (PreInstalledAppsService/template service keep their info-level skip line); DOWNGRADE/INVALID → one warn line; no UPGRADING→INSTALLED flip-flop, no revertStateToInstalledBestEffort. runInstallWithMetrics no longer counts APP_ALREADY_INSTALLED as app-upgrade/failed. Same exception message/code → failing-application-version-progression integration snapshot unchanged. New unit spec application-install.service.already-installed.spec.ts (3 cases: same version silent refusal, downgrade warn+metric, newer version still UPGRADING→INSTALLED). Tier-2 residual: boot/`install-pre-installed-apps` on a workspace with the bundled apps already installed shows only the PreInstalledAppsService info line.

userStories.title: P4C.5 task due-date overlay on /calendar (read-only, opens the task in the native side panel)
userStories.description: As a calendar user, I want my tasks' due dates to show on the calendar days they fall on, visibly distinct from scheduled events, so that I can see deadlines next to my schedule and open the task in one click without the calendar ever turning a deadline into an event.
userStories.completionNotes: Executor done (awaiting orchestrator). useCalendarTaskDueDates reads standard `task` rows (id/title/dueAt/status) with a dueAt range filter built in the viewer zone (getCalendarTaskDueQueryRange: start of first visible day inclusive, start of the day after the last exclusive; DST-aware), skipped when the overlay is hidden or the member lacks task read permission (useFindManyRecords already gates on it). groupCalendarTaskDuesByDay buckets by the due day in the viewer zone, skips null/unreadable/out-of-range due dates, dedupes, flags overdue (open + before today) vs done, orders open by due time/title and sinks done. CalendarTaskDueChip: dashed outline + IconCheckbox + Due/Overdue/Done state (never the event accent border), opens the task via useOpenRecordInSidePanel. Wired into month/week/day/agenda (agenda lists days that only have deadlines; empty states count deadlines), toolbar toggle 'Task due dates' (aria-pressed), non-blocking load error line. No write path, no schema/server change, works without Projects (dueAt is standard). 9 new cases; front calendar 21 suites / 221 tests green (scratch harness). Tier-2: /calendar browser proof.

userStories.title: P4C.5 quick-create a standard task from a calendar day (day + week views)
userStories.description: As a calendar user, I want to add a task due on a given day straight from the calendar, so that I can capture a deadline where I am planning without opening the Tasks page — and without the calendar scheduling or inviting anyone.
userStories.completionNotes: Executor done (awaiting orchestrator). 'Add task' on the day view header and an icon button per week-view day column open CalendarTaskQuickCreateDialog (labelled title input, autofocus, Escape cancels, 'Due <full date>' line, hint that nothing is scheduled). useCalendarTaskQuickCreate writes one standard `task` through useCreateOneRecord (native record path, pre-generated id, status TODO, dueAt = local noon of the chosen day via buildCalendarQuickTaskInput so the day holds for teammates within ±11h and round-trips through the overlay grouping); blank titles never submit. Buttons only render when the deadline overlay is shown and the member can create tasks (object permission canUpdateObjectRecords). FORBIDDEN vs generic error copy; success refetches the overlay and announces 'Task created'. No event row, no invitation, no schema/server change. 8 new cases; front calendar 22 suites / 229 tests green (scratch harness). Tier-2: /calendar browser proof.

userStories.title: M1: worker containers must not run bundled app provisioning (compose/coolify/podman) + server opt-out passthrough
userStories.description: As an operator, I want bundled A2E app provisioning to run exactly once per boot on the migrating server, so that worker containers never race it on an unmigrated schema or run a second concurrent install pass, and so that the documented DISABLE_BUNDLED_APP_PROVISIONING opt-out actually reaches the server.
userStories.completionNotes: Executor done (awaiting orchestrator). entrypoint.sh skips provisioning when DISABLE_DB_MIGRATIONS=true unless DISABLE_BUNDLED_APP_PROVISIONING=false forces it; every shipped worker (docker-compose, both coolify copies, podman-compose, manual podman) sets DISABLE_BUNDLED_APP_PROVISIONING=true; every server passes ${DISABLE_BUNDLED_APP_PROVISIONING:-} through (the documented opt-out was a no-op before). New provision-bundled-apps.deployment.spec.ts runs the real entrypoint under /bin/sh with stubbed yarn/psql (6 environments) + manifest guards: 10 failing at base, 15/15 after. Server tsgo exit 0, oxlint 0/0. Tier-2: compose/podman boot logs show provisioning on the server only; worker restart runs nothing.
